topic.title: Domain Adaptation and the Limits of Invariance
topic.overview: Domain adaptation transfers a predictor between distributions, often using source labels and little target supervision. Representations that make domains look similar are appealing, but may erase information needed to distinguish classes. The central question is which differences should be removed and which reflect genuine changes in the prediction problem.
topic.whyItMatters: Matching feature distributions alone does not guarantee target accuracy. Conditional shifts and different class proportions can make source performance and invariance compatible with poor transfer, so assumptions about the source–target relationship matter.
topic.evolution: A 2006 representative formalizes representation tradeoffs through generalization bounds. Later methods learn and co-regularize alignments, while 2019 theory supplies counterexamples to invariance-only reasoning. Recent work explores multi-source biomedical adaptation and synthetic noise domains. These extensions change the available supervision without eliminating the need to justify what transfers.
openQuestions: How can adaptation detect label or conditional shifts without enough target labels?
Which alignment objectives preserve useful distinctions across multiple target domains?
